chunks: Via his chain to Umar ibn Udhayna from Zurara from Abi Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about the sick person – how does he prostrate? He said: on a small palm-leaf mat or on a hand-held fan or on a tooth-stick which is raised to him [made to touch his forehead], and it is better than gesturing [without the forehead touching anything], verily the one who dislikes prostrating on the hand-held fan dislikes it because of the idols which used to be worshiped apart from Allah, and we never worship anything besides Allah ever – so prostrate on the fan and on the tooth-stick and on a piece of wood.
ai.seo_question: How should a sick person perform prostration if they cannot touch the ground directly?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) clarifies that a sick person may prostrate on raised objects like a palm-leaf mat, fan, or tooth-stick, which is superior to mere gesturing (imā'). He explains that the historical dislike for using fans stems from their pre-Islamic association with idol worship, not from inherent impurity, affirming that Muslims worship only Allah. This ruling underscores the Shia principle of distinguishing between ritual purity and cultural associations in fiqh.
